testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are called "headache racks." They protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Steer with one hand to keep the other hand free.

questions.explanation: In work zones, follow posted speed limits. Slow down if road or weather conditions are poor. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: If a person commits two serious traffic violations within a three-year period, they will:

options.text: Lose their CDL for at least one week.
Lose their CDL for at least 30 days.
Lose their CDL for at least 60 days.
Lose their CDL for at least two years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose their CDL for at least 60 days.
questions.explanation: Two serious traffic violations in three years will result in losing your CDL for at least 60 days.

questions.question: When an engine is started:

options.text: The brakes should be locked up.
Warning lights should come on and then quickly turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should come on and then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual brake system, a driver should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure that fuel reaches the engine.
Wait to begin driving until the air compressor builds up a minimum pressure of 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Begin driving just after the vehicle starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times to build pressure, then begin driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait to begin driving until the air compressor builds up a minimum pressure of 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, wait for the air compressor to reach 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: How does doubling your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph affect your vehicle's braking distance?
questions.explanation: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance multiplies by four. Higher speeds increase your vehicle's hitting force and braking distance.

questions.question: If a tire fails, the driver should:

options.text: Keep one hand on the steering wheel and use their other hand to wave to other drivers.

questions.explanation: If a tire fails, braking can cause you to lose control. Unless you must brake to avoid a crash, stay off the brakes until your vehicle slows down. Then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: When driving with a load, the driver should:

options.text: Stop and check on the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
Ask other drivers about the condition of their load.
Use the side mirrors only to check on the cargo.
Not check on the cargo if it was secured properly before starting the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check on the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
questions.explanation: Check cargo and securing devices before starting your trip. During the trip, check them within the first 50 miles, then every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: When nearing a construction worker who is close to the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until the construction is complete before proceeding.

questions.explanation: In work zones, reduce your speed when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: During exercises that are not the straight line backing exercise, you may exit your vehicle to check its position no more than:
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during basic control skills tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can look once. For other exercises, you can look twice.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians do not see you. Be ready for them to suddenly move into your path. You may lightly tap your horn or flash your lights as you pass.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines during a vehicle inspection, which should NOT be true:

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection, listen for leaks in the air hoses. Make sure the air hoses and electrical lines are not cut, chafed, spliced, or worn. Check that air and electrical lines are not tangled, pinched, or dragging against tractor parts.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: The truck will not have any brakes.
The truck should be driven only at slow speeds.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will lack brakes on its left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the vehicle will still have normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: What can change the height of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower than usual. A vehicle is taller when carrying a light load than when carrying a heavy load. If your vehicle fits under an overpass when fully loaded, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab due to:

options.text: The wrong type of fuel being used.
A lack of oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If you are being tailgated, you should:
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space ahead of your vehicle so the driver can pass safely. Do not drive faster because the driver may continue to tailgate you, which increases danger.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube used to move air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part in the braking unit that allows air to move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device in an air brake system. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If testing a bus, keep contact with the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times are you permitted to exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you can exit your vehicle to check its position no more than one time.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a double combination vehicle with air brakes, leakage should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, do not drive the vehicle because it needs repairs.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps keep an engine working properly:
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your vehicle's cooling system. Despite its name, antifreeze helps your engine even in hot weather.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a warning signal activates if air tank pressure drops below 60 psi. This signal can be a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: During the on-road test, you are checked on traffic awareness. You should NOT:
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, check traffic regularly and use your mirrors often, especially at intersections. Look for pedestrians in all areas.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for any unusual noises.

questions.question: While driving, if you notice a safety or mechanical problem, you should:

options.text: Say nothing and hope it goes away.
Write a report about your concerns.
Avoid using that part and hope no one notices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report about your concerns.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day, you may need to write a report on the vehicle you drove. Report any problems that could affect safety or cause mechanical failure.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the maximum leakage rate during an applied leakage test is:
questions.explanation: Know the safe maximum air loss rate for your vehicle. A single vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than 3 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic pressure, you should do all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find an escape route like a ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: A driver with an open window in cold weather may be:
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who are drunk, sleepy, on drugs, or ill are hazards to others. An open window in cold weather may indicate impairment.

questions.question: When it is hard to see your vehicle, such as at dawn or dusk, you can help others by:

options.text: Waving your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When visibility is poor, turn on your headlights to low beam. If you have trouble seeing others, they have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distraction?
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention from driving is a dangerous distraction. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, and adjusting the radio or climate controls.

questions.question: Most CDL holders have ____ licenses.
questions.explanation: Most CDL holders who drive commercial vehicles across state lines are non-excepted drivers.

questions.question: A truck may need to stay below the legal weight limit when driving:
questions.explanation: It may not be safe to drive at full legal weight in poor weather or on mountain roads.

questions.question: A vehicle stopped at a green light may mean the driver:
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who are drunk, tired, using drugs, or sick can be dangerous. Stopping at a green light is one sign a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: Multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions are used:

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions give vehicles extra gears. They are usually controlled by a selector knob on the gear shift lever.

questions.question: Which one does NOT require a CDL?

options.text: Operating a truck with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
Operating a vehicle designed to carry 16 or more people, including the driver
Any size vehicle that requires hazardous materials warning signs

questions.explanation: A CDL is needed to operate a vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, a vehicle designed to carry 16 or more people including the driver, or any vehicle that must display hazardous materials warning signs.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection part of the skills test, you must:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to show your knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid level:

options.text: You may need to leave the engine running.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may need to leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: On some vehicles, the engine must be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving:

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
You can check from inside the vehicle.
You can check by looking at a reflection in a shiny surface.

questions.explanation: To check your lights before driving, set the parking brake, turn off the engine, remove the key, and take it with you. Turn on your low beams and flashers. Get out and check that all lights work.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is located in the air tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph in ideal conditions needs about ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph in ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Is not a cause for concern.
May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
Should be avoided by driving off the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is potentially dangerous. A cardboard box or paper sack might look harmless but could contain a hard or heavy object that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes made after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are acceptable on tires in the rear of the vehicle.
Are acceptable only when carrying a heavy load.

questions.explanation: Always check your wheels and rims before driving. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe to use.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because it is best to always accelerate very slowly.
So they do not lose control of their vehicle.
So the driver does not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So they do not lose control of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerating too quickly on a road with poor traction can cause you to lose control. In poor conditions, accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls how it works.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. The number and size of tanks in an air brake system varies by vehicle.

questions.question: When traveling down a downgrade, a vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.explanation: Gravity causes a vehicle to speed up on a downgrade. Before going downhill, choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: Which action will NOT result in losing your CDL for at least one year on a first offense?

options.text: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.04 percent or higher
Driving a commercial motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol
Refusing to take a blood alcohol test
Committing a misdemeanor while using a commercial motor vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Committing a misdemeanor while using a commercial motor vehicle
questions.explanation: Several offenses cause loss of your CDL for at least one year on a first offense. These include driving a commercial motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.04 percent or higher, driving while under the influence of alcohol, and refusing to take a blood alcohol test.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, you should NOT:

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle in front of you.
Avoid relying on tricks to help others pass.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your distance from the car ahead, avoid sudden moves, and do not use tricks like flashing your lights. Speeding up only makes things worse by keeping the tailgater at a higher speed.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light turns on while driving:

options.text: Braking will only work if enough air remains in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
You should drive normally and check the brake system later.
You should turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking will only work if enough air remains in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park your vehicle as soon as possible. You can only brake if enough air is left in the tanks.
